title: Quick check: Pure Components and Render Purity

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the purpose of “Pure Components and Render Purity”?
options: The concept allows application code to mutate React-managed DOM and state directly.
Pure rendering logic should handle non-OK responses and represent loading, success, empty, and failure states.
The concept removes the need to consider error states or accessibility.
The browser will infer all application behavior even if inputs and state are contradictory.
questions.answer_key: Pure rendering logic should handle non-OK responses and represent loading, success, empty, and failure states.
questions.explanation: The correct choice is grounded in Pure Components and Render Purity: Pure rendering logic should handle non-OK responses and represent loading, success, empty, and failure states.

questions.prompt: Which practice is most reliable when applying Pure rendering logic?
options: Check response.ok before parsing success data and handle cancellation or out-of-order responses.
Skip validation because a successful render proves that the application is correct.
Store duplicate copies of every value so each component can change it independently.
Optimize by adding every available Hook without measuring the result.
questions.answer_key: Check response.ok before parsing success data and handle cancellation or out-of-order responses.
questions.explanation: The correct choice is grounded in Pure Components and Render Purity: Check response.ok before parsing success data and handle cancellation or out-of-order responses.

questions.prompt: What should you verify before considering “Pure Components and Render Purity” complete?
options: Check only whether the file exists; syntax and runtime behavior do not matter.
Assume a client-side check proves that a remote service accepted the change.
Rely only on a screenshot of the happy path and never repeat the test.
Verify the documented result with a normal example and at least one boundary, loading, or failure case.
questions.answer_key: Verify the documented result with a normal example and at least one boundary, loading, or failure case.
questions.explanation: The correct choice is grounded in Pure Components and Render Purity: Verify the documented result with a normal example and at least one boundary, loading, or failure case.
